exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

Which brand would you recommend for a high-protein snack, and why?
reviewed_answer:
Good Culture 2% Simply Cottage Cheese is my top pick for a high-protein snack in the U.S. It delivers about 14 g of protein per 1/2-cup serving, uses a short, simple ingredient list, and has a thick, creamy texture that makes it satisfying on its own or with fruit and nuts.

Why it stands out

Protein density: At roughly 14 g per half cup, it is among the higher-protein mainstream cottage cheeses, comparable to other strong options such as Clover Sonoma.

Simple formulation: Good Culture’s “Simply” line is typically made with cultured milk, cream, salt, and live active cultures—no gums, starches, or added sugars—so you get protein without unnecessary additives.

Snack-friendly texture: Its rich, small-curd style works well eaten straight from the container, spread on toast, or paired with berries; reviewers have also rated it highly for flavor and texture.

Widely available: It is sold in many U.S. supermarkets, making it a practical repeat purchase.

Good alternatives
Brand	Best for	Protein
Good Culture 2% Simply	Best overall high-protein snack; simple ingredients and creamy texture	~14 g per 1/2 cup 

Daisy 4%	Classic, widely available, mild flavor	13 g per 1/2 cup 

Clover Sonoma Organic	Organic preference; good calcium source	14 g per 1/2 cup 

Breakstone’s Live Active Low-Fat	Portable single-serve cups	12 g per serving 

If your priority is maximum protein per calorie, choose a 2% or low-fat version rather than 4% whole-milk cottage cheese. If you prefer the richest flavor and don’t mind a bit more fat, Daisy 4% is a very solid, widely available choice.
